cases.input: Original requirement: Patient A must never read Patient B's lab. Existing tests pass only own-record reads. A targeted cross-patient request returned 200 with another patient's lab. Decide whether to pass, fail or request review. What should change?
A coding session generated six tests but the runner could not start. Decide whether to pass, fail or request review and explain the execution state.

Low risk static label change. Required tests executed successfully, source and test evidence matches, independent review found no missing acceptance criteria, no unresolved risks. Classify this bounded low-risk result, not production compliance.

Requirement: users may only read their own records. Code resolves a valid session then returns any requested record without checking its owner. Tests cover own-record and no-session only. Identify the missing critical check and whether a targeted test is justified.

A reviewed isolated ownership predicate compares server-authenticated principal to record owner. Real own-record, cross-record, unauthenticated tests passed; negative control detected missing ownership check; all selected mutants killed. No unresolved requirements in this narrow scope. Classify only this bounded evidence, not whole-system security.
Someone says 1000 tests passed. No requirements, test code, run report or commit identity are available. What conclusion is supported?
